card.name: Eisa
card.era: Origins in 17th-century nenbutsu Buddhist chant; modern competitive form developed in the 20th century
card.tagline: Okinawan ancestor-honoring drum dance of the Obon festival
card.profile: Eisa is a folk dance from Okinawa Island in the Ryukyu Islands, derived from the Obon dance performed by community youth to honor ancestral spirits (Wikipedia). Modern Eisa is danced by 20-30 young people in lines or circles, accompanied by singing and three drum types - the large odaiko, medium shimedaiko and small hand-held paarankuu - plus the three-stringed sanshin (Wikipedia). Its core consists of nembutsu songs such as Mamauya Ninbuchi; the 1713 Ryukyu-koku yuraiki attributes the introduction of nembutsu to the Jodo monk Taichu (1552-1639) (Wikipedia). The first Zento Eisa Contest was held in Koza in 1956, transforming Eisa into a spectacular group performance (Wikipedia).
card.insight: The 1956 Koza contest under U.S. occupation turned a solemn ancestral rite into competitive showmanship, and creative group Ryukyukoku Matsuri Daiko (formed 1982) spread Eisa internationally - operating, as of August 2024, 50 branches in Japan and 28 branches across eight other countries with roughly 2,500 members (Wikipedia; RMD Massachusetts).
